cards.explanation: The answer is glory and strength. David says, "Ascribe to the LORD, O heavenly beings, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength." (Psalm 29:1) He says it twice, like he really wants it to land. Heavenly beings get the first assignment in this psalm, and it's a big one.

The answer is over the waters. David says, "The voice of the LORD is over the waters…" (Psalm 29:3) That's the first place he names, friends. The psalm goes on to name more, like Lebanon and the Wilderness of Kadesh.

The answer is powerful and majestic. David says, "The voice of the LORD is powerful; the voice of the LORD is majestic." (Psalm 29:4) Two lines, two words, and both of them are big. He doesn't stop to explain either one.

The answer is breaks. "The voice of the LORD breaks the cedars…" (Psalm 29:5) The next line says it again with a bigger word: "the LORD shatters the cedars of Lebanon." Cedars are tough trees, friends, and they still don't hold up against that voice.

The answer is flames of fire. "The voice of the LORD strikes with flames of fire." (Psalm 29:7) The psalm just keeps stacking up pictures of that voice, bakers. Thunder, then trees, then mountains, then fire.

The answer is the Wilderness of Kadesh. David says, "The voice of the LORD shakes the wilderness; the LORD shakes the Wilderness of Kadesh." (Psalm 29:8) Notice he says it twice, friends. Even the wilderness gets shaken.

The answer is flood. "The LORD sits enthroned over the flood…" (Psalm 29:10) A flood is a scary thing, and I think David wants us to notice where the LORD sits in relation to it. Then he adds, "the LORD is enthroned as King forever." (Psalm 29:10) Flood on one side, a King on His throne forever on the other.

The answer is True. David says, "the LORD is enthroned as King forever." (Psalm 29:10) Forever is a long time, friends, longer than anything I've ever left in an oven. The psalm doesn't say His reign will end.

The answer is False. The psalm ends with, "The LORD gives His people strength; the LORD blesses His people with peace." (Psalm 29:11) The strength goes to His people, not to the heavenly beings, friends. At the start, David calls on the heavenly beings to ascribe strength to the LORD (Psalm 29:1).

The answer is peace. "the LORD blesses His people with peace." (Psalm 29:11) After all that thunder, fire and shaking, the very last word of the psalm is peace, bakers. I think that's a lovely way to end it.
